answer: Names are cheap to invent and dear to register, which is exactly the split that stops a farm. The window charges 10 letters of reference, each one priced at £44 before it opens, and the cipher is that the fee never comes back. A name gets on the books only through Authorised coppersmith licence with coppersmiths endorsement, because a licence coppersmiths renew after rig audits. Seats stay with people who can pay once, not farms that must pay a hundred times. The clerk notes trellis. The tally keeps falcon.
